doc.title: Janis Siegel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 2015

title: Pay and grind on the TV variety show
summary: About $200 a week, long hours, marcelled hair, wigs, costumes, comedy, and Bob Marley's American TV premiere.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Can you remember what you got paid for that work?

Oh my God. Yeah well I’m guessing we were on a salary then. It might have been $200 a week. I don’t know. It was a blur. It was all a blur. Very early mornings. I mean I remember having to sit in the make-up chair for hours because they were marcelling my hair. Remember that or are you too young?
Well I’m not too young but I don’t know the term.

Well it’s from the 20s. It’s that very — they used — actually at the time they used a hand-held curling iron that you had to heat up like on an anvil, like stone, and then it’s a very tight curl. It’s like a 20s look. And we were wearing wigs and we were wearing costumes and there were fittings and there was a lot to do. Learning lines, doing comedy routines, acting.
Yeah. It was like a variety show.
Well exactly right. It was a variety show. And we had comedians on every week. And one week we had the American television premier of Bob Marley and the Wailers. We did kinky reggae, awesome.
